## Services
- Adult Dentistry
  Comprehensive dental care services for adult patients, including preventive, restorative, and specialty services under one roof.
- Bone Grafting
  A preliminary procedure performed before dental implant placement to build up insufficient jawbone density.
- Dental Bridges
  Fixed restorations that replace one to three consecutive missing teeth using two dental crowns and pontics (artificial teeth).
- Dental Checkups and Cleanings
  Routine maintenance appointments to preserve your smile, including examination, digital X-rays, and professional cleaning.
- Dental Crowns
  Tooth-shaped caps cemented over injured teeth to simultaneously restore their functionality and enhance their appearance, made with lifelike tooth-colored materials.
- Dental Implants
  Small titanium posts surgically placed in the jawbone to replace the roots and crowns of missing teeth, supporting crowns, bridges, or dentures.
- Dental Sealants
  A clear protective coating applied directly to the surfaces of teeth to seal out bacteria, plaque, and tartar, protecting against decay.
- Dentures
  Custom prosthetic teeth used to replace missing teeth, available as partial, full, or implant-supported options.
- Digital X-Rays
  Modern digital radiography that captures clear images of underlying tooth structures more quickly, safely, and comfortably than traditional X-rays.
- Full Dentures
  Traditional removable dentures that replace an entire arch of missing teeth, held in place via natural suction on the gum line.
- Gum Disease Therapy
  A range of periodontal therapies to improve oral health and prevent lasting damage from gum disease, including scaling and root planing.
- Implant Bridge
  A dental bridge supported by titanium implant posts placed in the jawbone rather than by reshaping adjacent natural teeth.
- Implant Dentures
  Dentures supported directly to the jawbone via dental implants, providing greater stability and longevity than traditional dentures.
- Intraoral Cameras
  Slender cameras that capture crystal clear images of teeth visible above the gum line, allowing patients to see exactly what the dentist sees.
- Oral Surgery
  Comprehensive oral surgical services including tooth extractions, wisdom tooth extractions, and dental implant placement, performed in-house.
- Orthodontics
  Traditional braces and orthodontic treatment to straighten teeth, correct bite alignment issues, and improve oral health for adolescents and adults.
- Partial Dentures
  Prosthetics designed to fill gaps for patients missing some teeth, supported via metal clips clasping to nearby teeth.
- Pediatric Dentistry
  Dental care focused on the oral health of infants, children, and adolescents, including persons with special health care needs.
- Prosthodontics
  Specialty restorative dentistry focused on the restoration and replacement of teeth, including crowns, bridges, fillings, dentures, and root canal therapy.
- Root Canal Treatment
  A procedure to restore teeth after severe tooth decay or dental injuries by removing infected tissue, sanitizing, and sealing the tooth.
- Scaling and Root Planing
  A two-step deep cleaning procedure involving careful removal of built-up plaque and tartar trapped under the gums and smoothing of tooth roots to prevent future buildup.
- Special Needs Dentistry
  High-quality, comfortable dental care for children and adults with physical and/or intellectual disabilities.
- Tooth Extractions
  Removal of problematic teeth including simple extractions and surgical removals, performed in-house by board-certified specialists.
- Tooth-Colored Fillings
  Composite resin fillings that blend seamlessly with the natural color of teeth, used to restore tooth structure damaged by decay.
- Wisdom Tooth Extraction
  Surgical removal of wisdom teeth (third molars) to prevent impaction, crowding, cavities, and gum disease.
- Your Child's First Visit
  An introductory dental appointment for children that includes a tour of the office, digital X-rays, examination, cleaning, and oral hygiene education.

## Frequently Asked Questions
**Q:** What Should I Bring to My First Appointment?
**A:** Identification - photo identification, such as a driver's license. Insurance card - if you plan on using insurance. List of current medications - if any.

**Q:** When Should I Arrive at My Appointment?
**A:** You may arrive at your appointment time but if you would like to come 15 minutes before your scheduled appointment, this will allow us to finalize any paper work you may need.

**Q:** What Treatment Options Are Available?
**A:** At your child's initial orthodontic appointment, the orthodontist will carefully assess their smile and discuss the available treatment options to determine the most suitable one. Various solutions are available to address a wide range of dental issues, such as traditional metal braces.

Additionally, the rising popularity of clear aligners has introduced another viable treatment choice in recent years. Following a thorough examination, the orthodontist will guide you through the different options and help you make an informed decision for your child's orthodontic treatment.

**Q:** How Long Will Treatment Last?
**A:** The duration of orthodontic treatment varies depending on several factors, making it difficult to provide a specific answer. The type of orthodontics being used, the age of the patient, and the patient's adherence to the treatment plan all play a role in determining the timeline.

Typically, treatment is completed within one to two years. However, in some cases, young children may require multiple treatment phases to achieve optimal results. It is important to consult with your little one's orthodontist, as they will give you a better estimate of the duration of your child's treatment.

**Q:** Are There Specific Foods My Child Needs to Avoid?
**A:** Orthodontic treatment often comes with a set of dietary restrictions, and it is crucial to follow them for the success of your child's treatment. While clear aligners can be removed during meals, metal braces have stricter limitations.

Nonetheless, it's important to encourage your child to exercise caution with their food choices. Certain items, such as popcorn, hard or chewy candies, and similar foods, have the potential to damage orthodontic appliances.

**Q:** Is Orthodontic Treatment Painful?
**A:** When braces or other orthodontic appliances are initially placed, your child may experience temporary discomfort or irritation. However, it's important to note that this sensation should subside over time.

To help your child adjust to wearing orthodontics, there are several measures you can take to alleviate any discomfort they may experience. Encouraging saltwater rinses, over-the-counter pain relievers, and the application of orthodontic wax to address any protruding wires or brackets can provide relief.

**Q:** How Much Will Treatment Cost?
**A:** The cost of orthodontic care is primarily determined by the type of treatment and the duration of the treatment plan. Due to the significant variation in orthodontic costs, many practices collaborate with multiple insurance providers to offer coverage options.

Additionally, to ease the financial burden associated with orthodontic treatment, many practices provide other payment options, such as financing. Dental financing options are available to help individuals manage the cost of dental treatments and procedures by providing flexible payment plans.

**Q:** Do Dental Crowns Feel Natural?
**A:** After several days of receiving your brand-new dental crowns, your restoration should start to feel increasingly more natural. Your dental cap will be constructed out of durable materials like composite resin and porcelain, which can withstand the everyday pressures of chewing, similar to your natural pearly whites. This means it shouldn't feel strange to eat with your dental crowns, especially since your restorations will be created to match the rest of your smile. With a comfortable and personalized fit, you will hardly tell the difference!

**Q:** How Long Do Dental Crowns Last?
**A:** In most cases, dental crowns can last as long as 5 to 15 years, and this mainly depends on how well they are taken care of. The lifespan of the restoration can also depend on the kind of material it's made from. For instance, metal crowns often go for longer than metal-free ones. Of course, you'll want to consider other factors like diet, oral hygiene, and bad habits that can wear down the restoration, such as nail-biting, teeth grinding, and smoking. Additionally, a dental crown placed on a front tooth can often have a longer lifespan than those placed on the back molars since they won't be worn down as much from chewing.

**Q:** Are Dental Crowns Covered by Insurance?
**A:** The majority of dental insurance companies offer partial coverage for restorative treatments, including dental crowns. Since they're often considered "medically necessary," you can typically expect around 50% of the total cost of the service to be covered by your insurer, so long as you paid the deductible and before you've passed your annual maximum. Don't forget that every insurance policy will be different from patient to patient, so it's a good idea to verify the specifics of your plan with your provider so that you know the details and there are no surprises. You can also speak with our front desk team, who will be more than happy to walk you through the specifics while also filing claims on your behalf for a smoother experience.
